s1.quote: The Hole Depth: 15 – 21 metres Location: Outer Gneerings Certification Required: Open Water Average visibility: 10m (summer), 15m (winter) … The hole offers the only safe swim through on the Mooloolaba Coral Reefs.

highlights.text: Only safe swim-through on the Mooloolaba reefs
Wobbegongs and groupers live in the bowl below

s1.quote: MKVI Depth: 10 – 17 metres Location: Outer Gneerings Certification Required: Open Water Average visibility: 10m (summer), 15m (winter) … the ledge that runs in an East – West direction

highlights.text: Ledge running east-west makes navigation easy
Anemones, clownfish and Christmas tree worms
Mini cave with wobbegongs and slipper lobsters

sites.name: Pinnacles

s1.quote: Pinnacles Depth: 15 – 24 metres … There are 2 pinnacles that rise from the sand in 24 metres. The top of one pinnacle is 16 metres and the other rises to 14 metres.

highlights.text: Massive blue anemone on one pinnacle

sites.depthNote: Two pinnacles from 24 m sand; tops at 16 m and 14 m

s1.quote: Manta Bommie Depth –5-15m Difficulty level –OW/ADV/SNO … migrating manta rays stop off to access the cleaning stations on several shallow bommies

s2.quote: Manta Bommie … cleaning station for the migratory Manta Rays … (November – April). … Depth 5 to 16m Current Minimal to Medium Visibility 5 to 30m

s3.quote: Between November and April, with visibility at times exceeding 15 metres, Manta Bommie is home

highlights.text: Manta ray cleaning station, November to April
Leopard sharks and guitarfish

hazards.text: Current and swell can make the dive challenging

summary.text: A group of rocky outcrops a short boat ride off Point Lookout where migrating manta rays visit shallow cleaning stations through the summer. Leopard sharks, rays and turtles also turn up. Depths are shallow, but current and swell can make it demanding.

s1.quote: Turtle Cave Depth –10-30m Difficulty level –ADV Located on the NW side of Flat Rock … grey nurse sharks

s2.quote: Flat Rock – Turtle Caves Reaching depths between 12-30 metres, Turtle Caves … the grey nurse shark

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks in winter
Batfish schools, barracuda and turtles
Eagle ray fevers and humpback whales in winter

s1.quote: Shag Rock, with depths between 6 and 20 metres is complete of rocky reefs and coral gardens

highlights.text: Rocky reefs and coral gardens

s1.quote: Shark Alley Depth –18-26m Difficulty level -ADV … large numbers of grey nurse sharks reside on the sand channel

s2.quote: Shark Alley … grey nurse shark population that inhabit this site from June – October … Experience Level Advanced

s3.quote: Shark Alley is a more advanced dive than either Turtle Caves or Shag Rock

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks in two sand channels, June to October
Rays, turtles and wobbegongs

summary.text: The grey nurse shark hotspot on the eastern edge of Flat Rock, where sharks gather over two parallel sand channels in winter. It is rated an advanced dive because it starts deep and can carry current.

s1.quote: The Nursery Depth –4-18m Difficulty level –OW/SNO A magic site … lots of juvenile fish and pretty plant and coral life

s2.quote: Flat Rock – The Nursery … The depth ranges between 4m and 20m

s3.quote: The Nursery … the shallowest of Flat Rock’s dive sites … making it a perfect place for beginner divers

highlights.text: Juvenile fish, coral and macro life
Occasional hammerhead passing through

summary.text: The shallowest of the Flat Rock dives, on its south-west corner, with coral gardens, juvenile fish and macro life rather than big pelagics. A little current is normal but easy to use, so it works well for beginners.

s1.quote: Amity Point Depth –5-15m Difficulty level –OW/SNO A shore dive option … Hazards include fishing lines, boat traffic, tidal movement, and a large population of stonefish

hazards.text: Very tidal; dive about an hour before high tide

highlights.text: Wobbegongs, schooling fish, occasional dolphin

sites.name: Flat Rock - Blue Corner

s1.quote: Blue Corner Depth –28-45m Difficulty level –Master Diver/XR … The top of the reef area is around 28m, dropping down to 40-45m on the sand. Large bull sharks frequent the area … can be prone to current

highlights.text: Large bull sharks and varied reef life

hazards.text: Prone to current; free ascent skills needed

sites.depthNote: Reef top about 28 m, dropping to 40-45 m on sand

s1.quote: Terrigal Haven Terrigal, NSW Water temp 15–20 °C Visibility Variable Depth 5-12 … With a maximum depth of around 12 metres … perfect for beginners

s2.quote: Terrigal Haven (15m) - A popular shore dive and nursery for fish and other marine life.

s3.quote: Visibility at Terrigal Haven averages between 8 and 12 metres but can reach 15 metres on calm days … Tidal movement is minimal

highlights.text: Giant cuttlefish in winter, blue gropers
Port Jackson sharks in breeding season

summary.text: A sheltered harbour dive beside the Terrigal boat ramp, shielded from southerly swell with minimal tide and a gentle sandy slope. Good for beginners, refreshers and macro photography, with cuttlefish, gropers and nudibranchs.

s1.quote: Skillion Cave (20m) - One of the best shore dives in NSW. You jump off the rock platform … enormous colony of Jewel Anemones

s2.publisher: Michael McFadyen's Scuba Diving Web Site
s2.quote: Skillion Cave … The depth is now almost 20 metres … any sort of swell from the east or north-east crashes right into the entry and exit points

highlights.text: Enormous colony of jewel anemones
Blue gropers inside the crack

hazards.text: East or north-east swell breaks on entry and exit

summary.text: A shore dive from the rock platform north of Terrigal Haven that follows a wall down to a crack in the reef with a boulder roof. It reaches about 20 m, and jewel anemones and gropers live inside. Swell from the east makes entry and exit unsafe.

s1.quote: Wave Break Island This man-made island … ideal for snorkelling and introductory diving. … The depth ranges from 0m at the beach to about 12m

s2.quote: Wave Break Island is where you’ll find scores of stunning colourful fish, coral, Wobbegongs and Grey Nurse Sharks.

highlights.text: Small fish on the northern rock wall
Wobbegongs and grey nurse sharks

hazards.text: Tidal; best dived on and after high tide

summary.text: A man-made breakwater island inside the Gold Coast Seaway that shelters divers from ocean swell. Shallow and protected, it is a standard site for introductory dives and snorkelling, with plenty of small fish, wobbegongs and sometimes grey nurse sharks.

s1.quote: As it’s an estuary entrance, the best time to dive is at the top of high tide when the current slows, and the water is clearest. … The North Wall offers most pelagic (open sea) fish activity

s2.quote: Gold Coast Seaway - The Spit Often referred to as the best dive site of any Australian city. … North Wall – schools of pelagic fish, wobbegong and whaler sharks

s3.quote: Gold Coast Seaway – Queensland’s Favourite Shore Dive

highlights.text: North Wall: pelagic fish, wobbegongs, whaler sharks

hazards.text: Tidal current; dive at high-tide slack

summary.text: An estuary-mouth shore dive at the end of The Spit, split into the South Wall, North Wall and pipes. Tide drives everything: go at high-tide slack for the clearest water, then expect wobbegongs, pelagics and rays along the walls.

sites.name: Wonder Reef On The Gold Coast

s1.quote: The reef varies in depth from 8 meters to 30 meters making it ideal for a range of diver levels.

s2.quote: Nine huge spiral-shaped structural reefs float about 8m beneath the surface. They are held in place by huge chains that descend about 25m to the ocean floor

highlights.text: Nine buoyant spiral reefs floating above the seabed

summary.text: An artificial dive site off The Spit made of nine large spiral structures that float on chains above the seabed. They start around 8 m and the seabed lies at roughly 25-30 m, so there is something for most levels.
